Affenpinschers.description: A wiry, monkey-faced German ratter once kept in kitchens and stables to hunt down rodents by the fistful.

Afghan Hounds.description: An ancient Afghan mountain sighthound built to run down gazelle over brutal terrain, wrapped in a coat thick enough to survive winter there.

Airedale Terriers.description: The largest terrier breed, a Yorkshire river-hunter nicknamed the 'King of Terriers' that later served as a messenger dog in WWI trenches.

Akitas.description: A powerful Japanese mountain dog bred to hold bear and boar at bay, later immortalized worldwide as a symbol of loyalty.

Alaskan Malamutes.description: An Arctic freight-hauling breed built by the Mahlemut people for raw pulling power over long distances, not sprint speed.

American English Coonhounds.description: A fast, loud-voiced American hound developed for chasing raccoons up trees through the night on nothing but scent and nerve.

American Eskimo Dogs.description: A crisp white Spitz-type dog that toured Depression-era America as a circus tightrope performer before becoming a family companion.

American Foxhounds.description: A Colonial-era scent hound refined in part by George Washington's own kennels for mounted fox hunts across open country.

American Hairless Terriers.description: A rat terrier line that went hairless through a single spontaneous mutation on a Louisiana farm in the 1970s, then bred true from there.

American Staffordshire Terriers.description: A muscular, big-hearted American original, refined for a stocky build and a people-first temperament that belies its athletic strength.

Anatolian Shepherd Dogs.description: A Turkish livestock guardian bred for millennia to think for itself on the steppe, bonding to the flock as much as to its handler.

Australian Cattle Dogs.description: Bred by crossing herding dogs with the dingo to produce a tireless, low-nipping drover that could push cattle across the Outback.

Australian Shepherds.description: Despite the name, a herding breed shaped on American ranches to work sheep with an intense, independent eye.

Australian Terriers.description: A scrappy, rough-coated Australian terrier bred small enough to go down a burrow after vermin — and snakes — on remote farms.

Azawakhs.description: A whip-thin Sahelian sighthound kept by West African nomads to run down game and guard camp in brutal desert heat.

Barbets.description: A curly-coated French water retriever considered an ancestor breed behind several other European water dogs, built to work marshes and duck blinds.

Basenjis.description: A Central African hunting dog that doesn't bark, prized for driving game silently into nets with its curled tail held high.

Basset Fauve de Bretagnes.description: A short-legged, wiry-coated French scenthound bred to push rabbits out of the thick Breton undergrowth other hounds couldn't get through.

Basset Hounds.description: A short-legged scenthound with a nose second only to the Bloodhound's, deliberately built low and slow enough for hunters on foot to keep up.

Beagles (13 in. and under).description: The smaller of the two AKC Beagle sizes — a compact English scenthound bred to pack-hunt rabbits by nose.

Beagles (over 13 in.).description: The larger AKC Beagle size, with more leg for keeping pace over rough ground on a rabbit's scent trail.

Bearded Collies.description: A shaggy Scottish drover's dog bred to push cattle and sheep across the Highlands in all weather, coat and all.

Beaucerons.description: One of France's oldest sheepdog breeds, a large, powerful herder distinguished by double dewclaws on each hind leg.

Bedlington Terriers.description: A lamb-shaped terrier from England's coal country, crossed with sighthound blood for a rare mix of a placid look with real terrier speed and grit.

Belgian Laekenois.description: The rarest of Belgium's four shepherd varieties, a rough-coated herder once trusted to guard drying linen out in open fields.

Belgian Malinois.description: A short-coated Belgian shepherd variety that became the dog of choice for military and police units worldwide.

Belgian Sheepdogs.description: A solid-black, long-coated Belgian shepherd variety that carried messages and pulled machine-gun carts for the Belgian army in WWI.

Belgian Tervuren.description: A mahogany-and-black long-coated Belgian shepherd variety, bred from the same herding stock as its Malinois and Sheepdog cousins.

Bergamasco Sheepdogs.description: An Italian Alpine flock guardian whose coat felts into thick wool mats over its lifetime, doubling as armor against cold and predators.

Berger Picards.description: One of France's oldest and most rustic herding breeds, twice nearly wiped out by the World Wars fought across its home region.

Bernese Mountain Dogs.description: A tricolor Swiss farm dog bred to haul milk carts and drive cattle through Alpine passes, sturdy enough for real farm work.

Bichons Frises.description: A small white Mediterranean lapdog that swung between the courts of French nobility and the ropes of traveling street performers.

Biewer Terriers.description: A German offshoot of the Yorkshire Terrier, bred starting in the 1980s around a striking black, white, and tan piebald coat pattern.

Black and Tan Coonhounds.description: An American night hunter's hound, built from Bloodhound and Foxhound stock specifically to tree raccoons in the dark.

Black Russian Terriers.description: A Soviet military creation, engineered at the Red Star Kennel to guard installations through brutal winters other breeds couldn't handle.

Bloodhounds.description: An ancient tracking breed with a nose so reliable its trail evidence has been accepted in courts of law.

Bluetick Coonhounds.description: A mottled blue-coated Southern hound valued for its 'cold nose' — the ability to pick up a scent trail hours old.

Boerboels.description: A massive South African farm guardian bred to stand between a homestead and predators as large as leopards.

Border Collies.description: A border-country herding dog that controls sheep with a hypnotic stare rather than force, often called the most trainable breed there is.

Border Terriers.description: A wiry little terrier bred to run alongside mounted foxhounds all day, then squeeze underground to finish the job.

Borzois.description: A Russian aristocrats' sighthound, historically loosed in pairs to run down and hold wolves on the open steppe.

Boston Terriers.description: One of the first breeds developed entirely in the United States, refined in Boston from bull-and-terrier stock into a tuxedoed 'American Gentleman.'

Bouviers des Flandres.description: A rugged Belgian farm dog built to drive cattle and haul carts through Flanders weather, coat included.

Boxers.description: Descended from German boar- and bear-hunting mastiffs bred to grab and hold, later reshaped into a guard and military dog.

Bracchi Italiani.description: One of the oldest pointing breeds in Europe, the Bracco Italiano hunts with a loping, tireless gait and turns into a devoted homebody once the field work is done.

Briards.description: Bred to herd and guard French flocks unsupervised for days, the Briard carries a shaggy, weatherproof coat over a fiercely loyal, independent-minded heart.

Brittanys.description: Compact and endlessly eager, the Brittany was built by French sportsmen to point and retrieve all day without ever seeming to tire.

Brussels Griffons.description: Barely a foot tall, the Brussels Griffon descends from Belgian stable ratting dogs and still carries himself like the biggest personality in the room.

Bull Terriers (Colored).description: The Colored Bull Terrier carries the same egg-shaped head and mischievous, clownish personality as its white cousin, bred in patched and brindle coats for extra hardiness.

Bull Terriers (White).description: The original Bull Terrier line, bred pure white by Victorian fanciers chasing an almost sculptural silhouette, still carries the breed's mischievous streak.

Bulldogs.description: The Bulldog's wrinkled, determined face made it Britain's unofficial national mascot — and belongs today to one of the gentlest, most easygoing companions in the show ring.

Bullmastiffs.description: An English gamekeeper's watchful companion, bred to pair serious size and protective instinct with an unusually calm, steady nature at home.

Cairn Terriers.description: Small enough to squeeze into a Highland cairn after a fox, this terrier's whole body was engineered for digging, chasing, and never backing down.

Canaan Dogs.description: Israel's native pariah dog, once a self-sufficient desert survivor, still herds and guards with the sharp instincts of a breed that answered to no one.

Cane Corso.description: An Italian farm guardian whose name translates to 'bodyguard dog' — an athletic, watchful protector that's deeply loyal to its own family.

Cardigan Welsh Corgis.description: The older of the two Corgi breeds, the Cardigan drove cattle by nipping at heels and dodging kicks, and kept the long, fox-like tail its cousin lacks.

Cavalier King Charles Spaniels.description: Named for the British king rarely seen without one underfoot, the Cavalier has spent centuries perfecting the art of being an irresistible lap companion.

Cesky Terriers.description: Bred behind the Iron Curtain by a Czech geneticist who wanted a quieter, silkier earthdog, the Cesky hunts vermin with none of the usual terrier racket.

Chihuahuas (Long Coat).description: The flowing-coated Chihuahua carries the same outsized confidence as its smooth cousin, tracing back to a small companion dog of Mexico.

Chihuahuas (Smooth Coat).description: The world's smallest breed by AKC standard, the Smooth Coat Chihuahua descends from a Mexican companion dog and never got the memo about its size.

Chinese Crested.description: Bred as a hairless companion and ratter aboard trading ships, the Chinese Crested comes in two coats, bare-skinned and 'powderpuff,' from the very same litters.

Chinese Shar-Pei.description: One of China's oldest breeds, known for a dignified, independent temperament and the loose, sandpaper-textured wrinkles that make it instantly recognizable.

Chinooks.description: New Hampshire's official state dog, developed by a single 20th-century musher to pull sleds with a freight breed's power and a family dog's temperament.

Chow Chows.description: An ancient Chinese breed used for hunting, herding, and pulling carts, the Chow Chow is one of the few dogs with a naturally blue-black tongue.

Cirnechi dell’Etna.description: Bred for millennia on the slopes of Sicily's Mount Etna to course rabbits over volcanic rock, the Cirneco hunts by sight, scent, and sound at once.

Collies (Rough).description: Made famous by Lassie, the Rough Collie's flowing double coat sits over a Scottish sheepdog's brain built for reading a flock's every move.

Collies (Smooth).description: Bred from the same working stock as its long-coated cousin, the Smooth Collie herded cattle to market over distances the fancier coat wasn't suited for.

Coton de Tulear.description: Marooned on Madagascar for centuries, this cotton-soft companion breed developed in near-isolation until French colonists carried it home in the 20th century.

Dachshunds (Longhaired).description: The Longhaired Dachshund likely picked up its silky coat from spaniel crosses, softening the breed's badger-hunting bravado with a bit of elegance.

Dachshunds (Smooth).description: Built low and long to follow badgers straight into their own tunnels, the Smooth Dachshund is still, pound for pound, one of the boldest hunters in the AKC.

Dachshunds (Wirehaired).description: The wiriest of the three Dachshund coats came from terrier crosses, giving this variety a scruffier face and an extra dash of terrier boldness underground.

Dalmatians.description: Bred to trot for miles alongside carriages and fire wagons, the Dalmatian's spotted coat and boundless endurance made it a natural coaching-dog escort.

Dandie Dinmont Terriers.description: Named after a fictional farmer in a Walter Scott novel, this long-backed terrier was bred to go to ground after otter and badger in the Scottish borders.

Danish-Swedish Farmdogs.description: A hardy Scandinavian all-purpose farm dog, part ratter, part herder, part watchdog, that spent over a decade in the AKC's Foundation Stock Service before earning full recognition.

Doberman Pinschers.description: A German tax collector bred the Doberman specifically as a personal protection dog, and the breed has never lost its sharp, all-business edge.

Dogo Argentinos.description: Bred in Argentina to hunt wild boar and puma in packs, the all-white Dogo Argentino combines a big-game hunter's courage with a surprisingly affectionate home temperament.

Dogues de Bordeaux.description: France's oldest mastiff-type breed, the Dogue de Bordeaux was once a cart-puller and estate guardian, recognizable by the largest head, proportionally, of any dog breed.

English Foxhounds.description: Bred for centuries to run and give voice in a pack across the English countryside, the Foxhound was built for stamina alongside other hounds, not solo companionship.

English Toy Spaniels (Blenheim & Prince.description: Named for the Duke of Marlborough's Blenheim Palace, this red-and-white variety of England's royal lapdog has been a court favorite since the 17th century.

English Toy Spaniels (King Charles & Rub.description: Bred down from the same royal spaniel line, the black-and-tan King Charles and solid red Ruby varieties trade the Blenheim's markings for richer, solid coloring.

Entlebucher Mountain Dogs.description: The smallest and rarest of Switzerland's four sennenhund breeds, the Entlebucher was bred to drive cattle down alpine trails with a fearless, low-to-the-ground tenacity.

Finnish Lapphunds.description: Bred by the Sámi people to herd reindeer across the Arctic Circle, the Finnish Lapphund carries a weatherproof double coat built for temperatures most breeds couldn't survive.

Finnish Spitz.description: Finland's national dog was bred to 'bark-point,' treeing game birds and barking steadily until the hunter arrives, a trait still bred into every litter today.

Fox Terriers (Smooth).description: Bred to bolt foxes from their dens for mounted hunts, the Smooth Fox Terrier was shown as one breed with its wirehaired cousin until the AKC split them in 1985.

Fox Terriers (Wire).description: Sharing the same fox-bolting job and pedigree as its smooth-coated cousin, the Wire Fox Terrier wasn't split into its own AKC breed until 1985.

French Bulldogs.description: Descended from English toy bulldogs carried to France by lacemakers, the Frenchie's bat ears and compact build were refined entirely on the other side of the Channel.

German Pinschers.description: The direct ancestor of both the Doberman and the Miniature Pinscher, the German Pinscher itself nearly vanished after World War II before being rebuilt from a handful of survivors.

German Shepherd Dogs.description: Developed in a single decade by one German cavalry officer unifying regional herding dogs, the GSD became the template for nearly every modern working-dog program that followed.

Giant Schnauzers.description: Originally cattle drovers and brewery guards in Bavaria, the Giant Schnauzer is the largest and most serious-minded of the three schnauzer sizes.

Glen of Imaal Terriers.description: Bred to work Irish badger and fox dens in near silence, the Glen of Imaal Terrier is famously the quietest and most low-slung of the terriers.

Grand Basset Griffon Vendeens.description: A big voice on short legs, the Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen was built in France's Vendee region to trail hare across rough terrain all day.

Great Danes.description: Bred to run down wild boar at full gallop, the Great Dane earned its "Apollo of Dogs" nickname for a build that pairs raw power with unlikely elegance.

Great Pyrenees.description: Raised for centuries among Pyrenean flocks, this breed guards sheep not by herding but by simply outsizing and outlasting anything that threatens them.

Greater Swiss Mountain Dogs.description: The oldest and largest of the Swiss Sennenhund breeds, historically pulling carts of milk, cheese, and meat to market for Swiss farmers and butchers.

Greyhounds.description: Built purely for a flat-out sprint, the Greyhound remains one of the fastest land animals on earth despite millennia bred mainly as a companion of nobility.

Harriers.description: A scent hound sized between the Beagle and the Foxhound, the Harrier was built for mounted hare hunts that could run all day at a steady pack trot.

Havanese.description: Cuba's only native breed, the Havanese descends from shipboard lapdogs that became the pampered companion of colonial Havana's aristocracy.

Ibizan Hounds.description: An ancient sighthound from Spain's Balearic Islands, the Ibizan Hound hunts as much by ear and nose as by its famous vertical leap over garden walls.

Icelandic Sheepdogs.description: Iceland's only native breed, this spitz-type herder has driven sheep and ponies across the island's terrain since the Vikings' ships first brought its ancestors ashore.

Irish Terriers.description: Nicknamed the "Daredevil" by fanciers, the Irish Terrier served as a WWI messenger dog, pairing a fearless streak with real loyalty to its handler.

Irish Wolfhounds.description: The tallest of all AKC breeds, the Irish Wolfhound was bred to course wolves and Irish elk on the open plain, pairing a sighthound's speed with real mass.

Italian Greyhounds.description: A miniaturized sighthound favored by Italian nobility and painted into Renaissance courts, the Italian Greyhound keeps a full sprinter's stride at a fraction of the size.

Japanese Chin.description: Bred purely as a palace companion for Japanese royalty, the Japanese Chin carries a cat-like independence suited to lap life rather than the field.

Keeshonden.description: The Netherlands' barge dog, the Keeshond rode Dutch canal boats as a watchful companion, recognizable by the dramatic silver-and-black "spectacles" marking its face.

Kerry Blue Terriers.description: An Irish farm all-rounder that herded, guarded, and hunted vermin, the Kerry Blue Terrier is born black before fading to its signature blue-gray coat.

Komondorok.description: Hungary's corded livestock guardian, the Komondor's mop-like coat evolved to mimic a sheep at a glance while still shrugging off a wolf's bite on the range.

Kuvaszok.description: A Hungarian flock guardian with roots in royal kennels, the Kuvasz pairs an imposing white coat with an independent streak bred for working alone, far from any shepherd.

Lagotto Romagnolo.description: Italy's water retriever turned truffle hunter, the Lagotto Romagnolo shifted from marsh work to sniffing out prized fungi once Romagna's wetlands were drained.

Lakeland Terriers.description: Bred in England's rugged Lake District to bolt foxes from rock dens other terriers couldn't reach, the Lakeland Terrier is built narrow, wiry, and fearless.

Lancashire Heelers.description: A small Welsh Corgi-descended herder from Lancashire, England, this breed nipped at cattle's heels while staying low enough to the ground to dodge a kick.

Leonbergers.description: Bred in 19th-century Germany to resemble the lion on the town of Leonberg's crest, this giant breed pairs Newfoundland-style water instincts with Saint Bernard-scale mass.

Lhasa Apsos.description: Raised as sentinel dogs inside Tibetan monasteries, the Lhasa Apso relied on sharp hearing rather than size, alerting monks to visitors long before anyone reached the door.

Lowchen.description: Once called the "Little Lion Dog" for its traditional lion clip, the Lowchen was a European lapdog whose trim was originally meant to look fierce, not fashionable.

Maltese.description: One of the oldest toy breeds, the Maltese was bred on the island of Malta purely for companionship, prized by Mediterranean nobility for over two thousand years.

Manchester Terriers (Standard).description: Bred in industrial Manchester, England to course rats in the pits and rabbits in the field, the Standard Manchester Terrier is a sleek, black-and-tan ratting specialist.

Manchester Terriers (Toy).description: A scaled-down version of the ratting Manchester Terrier, recognized by the AKC a full year before its Standard-sized counterpart and bred purely as a lap companion.

Mastiffs.description: Descended from war and guard dogs recorded in ancient Britain, the Mastiff's sheer mass made it one of history's most formidable estate and property guardians.

Miniature American Shepherds.description: Developed in the U.S. from small working-line herding stock, the Miniature American Shepherd keeps full ranch-dog drive and intelligence in a compact frame.

Miniature Bull Terriers.description: A scaled-down Bull Terrier with the same egg-shaped head and famously clownish, full-of-personality charm packed into a smaller frame.

Miniature Pinschers.description: Often mistaken for a small Doberman, the Miniature Pinscher actually predates it, bred in Germany as a barn ratter with its own high-stepping "hackney" gait.

Miniature Schnauzers.description: Bred down from the Standard Schnauzer as a German farm ratter, the Miniature Schnauzer is the only schnauzer size developed without terrier crosses.

Mudik.description: A Hungarian herding breed as comfortable driving cattle as chasing off wolves, the Mudi is prized at home for an all-purpose versatility American fanciers are only now discovering.

Neapolitan Mastiffs.description: An imposing Italian guardian breed whose heavy, wrinkled hide and calm, devoted temperament have made it a beloved, if enormous, family companion.

Nederlandse Kooikerhondjes.description: Dutch duck hunters, Kooikerhondjes lured waterfowl within net range by wagging their plumed, black-tipped tails along a canal-side blind, a technique called "kooiker."

Newfoundlands.description: Bred by Canadian fishermen to haul nets and pull swimmers from icy North Atlantic water, the Newfoundland's webbed feet and oily coat still make it a natural lifeguard.

Norfolk Terriers.description: Nearly identical in origin to the Norwich Terrier but for drop ears instead of prick ears, the Norfolk Terrier was bred as an East Anglian barn and stable ratter.

Norwegian Buhunds.description: A Viking-era farm dog still carved into Norwegian burial ship relics, the Buhund herded sheep and cattle and guarded the homestead in equal measure.

Norwegian Elkhounds.description: Norway's ancient hunting spitz, the Elkhound tracked and held moose at bay with sharp barking, giving hunters time to close in, a job it has done for millennia.

Norwegian Lundehunds.description: Bred on remote Norwegian cliffs to squeeze into puffin burrows, the Lundehund has six working toes per foot and joints flexible enough to fold its head back along its spine.

Norwich Terriers.description: One of the smallest working terriers, the prick-eared Norwich Terrier hunted rats around Cambridge stable yards and rode along in saddlebags between jobs.

Old English Sheepdogs.description: Despite the name, the Old English Sheepdog was bred more for droving cattle to market than tending sheep, with a shaggy coat built for outdoor English winters.

Otterhounds.description: Bred with a rough, oily, waterproof coat and webbed feet built to swim down otters in British rivers, the Otterhound remains one of the AKC's rarest breeds — and one of its most devoted fan bases.

Papillons.description: Named for their butterfly-shaped ears, Papillons descend from the toy spaniels painted into royal European portraits for four centuries.

Parson Russell Terriers.description: Bred by an English parson to go to ground after foxes, these terriers pack fearless, tireless energy into a compact frame.

Pekingese.description: Once so revered in the Chinese imperial court that stealing one was punishable by death, Pekingese carry themselves like small lions.

Pembroke Welsh Corgis.description: Low enough to duck a cow's kick, Pembroke Welsh Corgis drove cattle by nipping at heels and became a British royal fixture.

Petits Bassets Griffons Vendeens.description: Built with a wiry, weatherproof coat for crashing through the thorny Vendée brush of western France while trailing rabbits by scent.

Pharaoh Hounds.description: One of the few dogs that visibly blushes, its nose and ears flushing pink with excitement, the Pharaoh Hound has hunted rabbit on Malta for centuries.

Plott Hounds.description: Descended from German boar hounds brought to the Carolina mountains, Plott Hounds are the only AKC scent hound with no British ancestry.

Pointers.description: Among the AKC's original breeds, Pointers freeze mid-stride into a statuesque point the instant they wind game in the field.

Pointers (German Shorthaired).description: Bred in Germany as an all-purpose gun dog, German Shorthaired Pointers point, track, and retrieve equally well on land or in water.

Pointers (German Wirehaired).description: A harsh, wiry coat lets German Wirehaired Pointers push through thorny cover and cold water that would stop a shorthaired hunter cold.

Polish Lowland Sheepdogs.description: Hidden behind a shaggy fringe of hair, Polish Lowland Sheepdogs have herded livestock across the flatlands of Poland for over a thousand years.

Pomeranians.description: Shrunk down from sled-pulling spitz stock under Queen Victoria's breeding program, the fox-faced Pomeranian is a big dog's personality in miniature.

Poodles (Miniature).description: Bred down from the water-retrieving Standard Poodle, the Miniature keeps the same sharp intelligence in a more compact, apartment-friendly frame.

Poodles (Standard).description: Standard Poodles were bred as water retrievers in Germany and France, and their trademark clipped coat was originally functional, not fashion.

Poodles (Toy).description: The smallest of the three Poodle sizes, the Toy was bred down from the water-retrieving Standard into a lapdog with the same sharp mind.

Portuguese Podengo Pequenos.description: One of Portugal's oldest breeds, the small Podengo Pequeno hunts rabbits in packs using sight, scent, and hearing all at once.

Portuguese Water Dogs.description: Portuguese fishermen once relied on this breed to herd fish into nets and swim messages between boats, a true working retriever of the sea.

Pugs.description: Bred purely for companionship in the palaces of ancient China, the Pug's wrinkled face and curled tail later made it the mascot of Dutch royalty.

Pulik.description: The Puli's dense, corded coat looks like dreadlocks but functions as all-weather armor for a dog built to herd sheep across the Hungarian plains.

Pumik.description: A Hungarian herder with corkscrew ears and a springy, curly coat, the Pumi is famously vocal, bred to bark livestock into line.

Pyrenean Shepherds.description: The tiny counterpart to the massive Great Pyrenees, this quick, wiry French herder moved flocks through the same mountain passes for centuries.

Rat Terriers.description: An all-American farm dog built for vermin control, the Rat Terrier's name is credited to Theodore Roosevelt after one cleared a White House rat problem.

Redbone Coonhounds.description: Immortalized in 'Where the Red Fern Grows,' the solid-red Redbone Coonhound was bred in the American South to trail and tree raccoons at night.

Retrievers (Chesapeake Bay).description: Descended from shipwrecked Newfoundland-type pups rescued off Maryland, the Chesapeake Bay Retriever's oily, waterproof coat was bred for icy bay waters.

Retrievers (Curly-Coated).description: The oldest of the retriever breeds, its tight, curly coat sheds water and thorns alike, built for English gamekeepers working rough cover.

Retrievers (Flat-Coated).description: Developed as a Victorian gentleman's do-it-all gun dog, the Flat-Coated Retriever is famous for staying puppyishly cheerful well into old age.

Retrievers (Golden).description: Bred on a Scottish Highland estate by a lord chasing the perfect gun dog, the Golden Retriever's soft mouth can carry an egg without cracking it.

Retrievers (Labrador).description: Despite the name, Labrador Retrievers originated in Newfoundland, where they hauled nets and retrieved escaped fish alongside working fishermen.

Retrievers (Nova Scotia Duck Tolling).description: Nicknamed the 'little river duck dog,' this fox-colored retriever lures curious ducks into range by playing fetch along the shoreline.

Rhodesian Ridgebacks.description: Bred in southern Africa to track lions and hold them at bay until hunters arrived, marked by a ridge of backward-growing hair down its spine.

Rottweilers.description: Descended from Roman drover dogs, Rottweilers later pulled butchers' meat carts through the German town that gave the breed its name.

Russell Terriers.description: A shorter-legged cousin of the Parson Russell, this terrier was bred to squeeze underground and bolt foxes straight into the hunt.

Russian Toys.description: Descended from English Toy Terriers gifted to Russian nobility, the breed nearly vanished behind the Iron Curtain before Soviet-era breeders revived it.

Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonkas.description: Developed in the Soviet Union from small Bichon-type companions, the Tsvetnaya Bolonka ('colored lapdog') is among the AKC's newest recognized breeds.

Salukis.description: Bred by Bedouin nomads to run down gazelle across the desert, Salukis were traditionally considered too sacred to sell, only given as gifts.

Samoyeds.description: Bred by Siberia's nomadic Samoyede people to herd reindeer and sleep curled against the family for warmth, hence its trademark upturned 'smile.'

Schipperkes.description: Belgian bargemen kept these small, foxy dogs aboard canal boats as fearless ratters and watchdogs, hence the name 'little captain.'

Scottish Deerhounds.description: Once restricted by law to Scottish nobility, the Deerhound's rough, wiry coat let it course red stags across the Highlands in any weather.

Scottish Terriers.description: A tenacious Highland earth-dog built to dig fox and badger from their burrows, later made a White House fixture by FDR's terrier Fala.

Sealyham Terriers.description: Bred all-white by a Welsh captain so hunters could tell dog from quarry underground, Sealyhams went to ground after badger, otter, and fox alike.

Setters (English).description: One of the oldest sporting breeds, English Setters get their name from the low crouch, or 'set,' they froze into for hunters working with nets.

Setters (Gordon).description: Developed on the Duke of Gordon's Scottish estate, the black-and-tan Gordon is the only setter breed with roots north of the English border.

Setters (Irish Red and White).description: The older, piebald ancestor of the solid-red Irish Setter, this breed nearly disappeared in the 20th century before a dedicated few revived it.

Setters (Irish).description: Bred in Ireland to range wide and fast across open moorland hunting birds, the Irish Setter's mahogany coat became as famous as its speed.

Shetland Sheepdogs.description: Bred down from working Collies on Scotland's remote Shetland Islands to herd sheep and ponies through brutal weather on scant rations.

Shiba Inu.description: Japan's oldest native breed, once flushing small game through dense brush, with an independent, almost cat-like self-possession still intact today.

Shih Tzu.description: Bred for centuries purely as a companion inside the Chinese imperial court — the entire job description was to be adored underfoot.

Siberian Huskies.description: Bred by Siberia's Chukchi people to haul light loads efficiently across vast distances, running on cooperation rather than dominance.

Silky Terriers.description: An Australian cross of Yorkshire and native terrier stock — lap-sized, but with a real terrier's nose for vermin underneath the silk.

Skye Terriers.description: Bred low and long to go to ground after otters and foxes on Scotland's Isle of Skye, coated for the weather it's named for.

Sloughis.description: An ancient short-haired sighthound of North Africa's Berber tribes, built for endurance coursing where a heavy coat would only slow it down.

Soft Coated Wheaten Terriers.description: An Irish farm all-rounder expected to herd, guard, and hunt vermin — without the hard edge bred into most other terriers.

Spaniels (American Water).description: Developed along the upper Midwest's rivers to retrieve from a small boat without swamping it — one of the few sporting breeds that's genuinely American.

Spaniels (Boykin).description: Bred in South Carolina to fit in a small johnboat for turkey and duck hunting in the swamp, and still rarely seen far outside it.

Spaniels (Clumber).description: The heaviest-boned spaniel, bred to move deliberately through thick cover, favoring thoroughness over speed.

Spaniels (Cocker) ASCOB.description: The solid-color division (any color but black) of a spaniel originally bred to flush woodcock from thick brush.

Spaniels (Cocker) Black.description: The solid-black division of the Cocker Spaniel, smallest of the sporting spaniels but built with the same flushing drive as its taller cousins.

Spaniels (Cocker) Parti.description: The parti-color division of the Cocker Spaniel, judged separately purely on coat pattern rather than any difference in build or work.

Spaniels (English Cocker).description: The taller original from which the American Cocker was bred down, still worked in Britain as an all-day upland flushing dog.

Spaniels (English Springer).description: Bred to "spring" game into the air for the gun — built for stamina across a full day's shooting, not one flush.

Spaniels (Field).description: A low, long-bodied spaniel bred to push through dense, thorny cover that would stop a shorter-legged dog cold.

Spaniels (Irish Water).description: The tallest spaniel, with a tight curling coat built for cold-water retrieving and a distinctive rat-like tail unlike any other.

Spaniels (Sussex).description: Bred to hunt at a slow, deliberate pace and bark on the trail, so a hunter on foot could actually keep up.

Spaniels (Welsh Springer).description: A distinct Welsh breed, not a springer variant despite the name, shaped by generations of isolation in the Welsh hills.

Spanish Water Dogs.description: A Spanish herding and retrieving all-rounder whose curly, cord-forming coat was deliberately left unbrushed to shed water working alongside fishermen.

Spinoni Italiani.description: An Italian pointing breed with a rough, wiry coat and a deliberately unhurried gait, built for a full day over rough ground.

St. Bernards.description: Bred by monks at the Alps' Great St. Bernard Hospice to find travelers buried in snow — built for endurance, not speed.

Staffordshire Bull Terriers.description: Bred down from old bull-and-terrier stock in England's Black Country, compact and muscular but prized as much for gentleness as toughness.

Standard Schnauzers.description: The original, medium-sized Schnauzer from which the Giant and Miniature were later bred — a German farm ratter and guard, not a lapdog.

Swedish Vallhunds.description: A low, Viking-era Scandinavian cattle-herder built to nip at heels and duck the kick, sharing surprising ancestry with the Welsh Corgi.

Teddy Roosevelt Terriers.description: A small American ratting and small-game terrier bred on farms in the country's midsection, among the AKC's newest recognized breeds.

Tibetan Mastiffs.description: Bred by nomadic herders on the Tibetan Plateau to guard flocks against wolves and leopards at altitude — a true livestock guardian, not a companion.

Tibetan Spaniels.description: Kept in Tibetan monasteries less as lapdogs than as small watchdogs perched on walls, alert to anyone approaching below.

Tibetan Terriers.description: Not a terrier by function at all — a Tibetan herding and companion breed that earned its very Western name purely from its shaggy, terrier-like look.

Toy Fox Terriers.description: Bred down in size from the Smooth Fox Terrier while keeping the full ratting instinct — a working terrier at lapdog scale.

Treeing Walker Coonhounds.description: A fast, cold-nosed American scent hound bred to run raccoons to ground, prized above all for a distinctive, far-carrying voice.

Vizslas.description: A Hungarian pointer-retriever bred to hunt close to a single gun rather than range wide — part of why they rarely leave a person's side.

Weimaraners.description: Bred by German nobility to hunt boar and deer, then repurposed as an all-around bird dog once big-game hunts declined.

Welsh Terriers.description: One of Britain's oldest terrier breeds, bred to go to ground after fox and badger in the Welsh hills, coated hard for the work.

West Highland White Terriers.description: Bred deliberately white so hunters in Scotland could tell the dog from the fox or badger it was chasing underground.

Whippets.description: Bred by English mill workers as an affordable small-scale sighthound for informal straight-line racing — a working-class Greyhound.

Wirehaired Pointing Griffons.description: A Dutch-bred all-around gundog with a coarse, weatherproof coat made specifically for hunting cold marshland that punished a smooth coat.

Wirehaired Vizslas.description: Bred later than the smooth Vizsla specifically to add a heavier, weatherproof coat for cold-weather and water work.

Xoloitzcuintli.description: One of the oldest breeds in the Americas, kept by pre-Columbian civilizations in three sizes, most famously a hairless variety.

Yorkshire Terriers.description: Bred by English mill workers to hunt rats in cramped textile-mill conditions — a world away from today's tiny show coat.

ALL OTHER BREEDS AND VARIETIES.description: The AKC's catch-all points bucket for breeds and varieties not individually broken out in the point schedule, typically newly recognized or lower-entry breeds.
